title: In 1978, a New York skyscraper was secretly fixed at night so it wouldn’t fall
body: Citicorp Center stands on four stilts under the middle of each side rather than at the corners. In 1978 its structural engineer, William LeMessurier, found that **quartering winds**, which hit a building diagonally, had never been checked, and that the braces’ joints had been bolted rather than welded, a change his office had approved. Diagonal winds raised the loads on four of the eight brace tiers by 40 percent; with the tuned mass damper off, a storm able to topple the tower had about a one-in-sixteen chance in any year. Welders plated the joints by night as Hurricane Ella approached, and a newspaper strike kept the story quiet until a 1995 New Yorker article.

slides.question: Picture 16 years with the sway damper of New York’s Citicorp Center off. In how many would a toppling storm be expected?
slides.explanation: About 1 year in 16, by engineer William LeMessurier’s 1978 estimate, with the tuned mass damper off; with it running, the odds fell to 1 in 55. A backup generator and welded plates fixed it.

slides.label: yearly odds of a storm able to topple the tower, with its damper off
slides.text: LeMessurier’s own 1978 estimate; with the damper working it was one in 55. A backup generator was installed, and repairs were completed in October 1978.

slides.heading: What went wrong
items: Stilts at mid-side, not the corners, so braces carry the load
Joints bolted, not welded as prescribed

slides.prompt: In June 1978 an engineering student’s thesis questioned the tower’s wind loads. Who wrote it?
slides.detail: Almost at the same time an architecture student, Lee DeCarolis, raised questions by phone. LeMessurier ran his own calculations on 24 July 1978 and found the danger.

slides.heading: Hero or cover-up?
slides.text: LeMessurier owned up to the flaw and got it fixed by October 1978, and many engineering schools and ethics educators use his story as an example of how to act ethically. Others criticise the secrecy: keeping the crisis hidden for almost 20 years delayed the lessons it held.

slides.question: Why were the repairs so little noticed at the time?
options: They were done in one night
slides.explanation: Welding went on at night while tenants worked by day, officials called it routine, and the city’s three major newspapers were on strike. The story became public in 1995.
